title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
synopsis: A concierge, a lobby boy, an inheritance scandal, a painting of a boy with an apple, and a long sled ride down an alpine slope.

nodes.text: A small lobby boy named Zero asks for a job from a desk.

choices.consequence: “Hire him” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Cunning.
There is no taking “Defer” back. Cautious shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: A dowager with a long fur, a tearful goodbye, a key to a safe.

choices.consequence: “Reassure her” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Heart.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Polite—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: A family of vultures and a clause that names you.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Brave.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Wise.

nodes.text: A small panel painting that everyone wants to keep nailed to the wall.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Cunning.

nodes.text: A papers check and a uniform with a scar from the Old War.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Speak up for Zero.” The story records the instinct as “Loyal” and carries it forward.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Joyful.

nodes.text: A border, a uniform, a smaller scar.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honor—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Wise.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You manage the Grand Budapest into a small renaissance and Zero takes over after you, and Agatha bakes things that make people cry on the lobby steps.
Decades later a lobby boy who once was small tells a young writer about a concierge with cologne and a pencil mustache, and a country he no longer recognizes.
The painting hangs in your suite forever and Dmitri spends his last years in a small angry apartment with a postcard of it on the mantel.
